At **512 dimensions**, the Matryoshka-trained PAIR model reaches a **MAR@100 of 0.444**, with a **relative retrieval latency of 0.65×** compared with the full 1024-dimensional embedding (Table 3, page 8).

- **Comparison with full dimensions:** The 1024-dimensional embedding scores a MAR@100 of 0.450 at 1.00× latency. Truncating to 512 dimensions therefore costs only 0.006 MAR@100 (page 8).
- **Storage:** The 512-dimensional variant uses 0.50× the storage of the 1024-dimensional embedding. Its intended use is "Standard retrieval" (page 8).
- **How latency is measured:** Relative latency is based on dimension-dependent retrieval cost plus a fixed serving overhead (Table 3 caption, page 8).
- **Same model:** All dimension variants come from one PAIR model trained with joint Matryoshka loss. The smaller embeddings are made by truncating the full one, not by training separate models (page 8).
